sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

"""Task B3 figures.

Reads results/runs.jsonl (phase=pilot rows, phase=confirm rows, and the
Part A dense seed-0 train/bench records) and writes:
  figures/acc_vs_sparsity.png
  figures/latency_vs_accuracy.png
  figures/size_vs_sparsity.png
  figures/CAPTIONS.md

Deterministic and re-runnable: reflects the current runs.jsonl contents.
Source CSVs are named in captions per figure.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

_REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO / "code"))

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

RESULTS = _REPO / "results"
FIGURES = _REPO / "figures"
RUNS = RESULTS / "runs.jsonl"

ARCHS = ("mlp", "cnn", "gcn")
METHODS = ("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4")
LAT_KEY = {"mlp": "batch_256", "cnn": "batch_256", "gcn": "full_graph"}
XLABEL = {
    "mlp": "achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero) [-]",
    "cnn": "achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero) [-]",
    "gcn": "achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero) [-]",
}
LAT_X = {
    "mlp": "median forward latency, batch 256 (ms, log scale)",
    "cnn": "median forward latency, batch 256 (ms, log scale)",
    "gcn": "median forward latency, full graph (ms, log scale)",
}


def _loads() -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for line in open(RUNS):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            out.append(json.loads(line))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
    return out


def _rows(recs: list[dict], phase: str, stage: str, status: str = "ok") -> list[dict]:
    return [
        r
        for r in recs
        if r.get("part") == "B" and r.get("phase") == phase
        and r.get("stage") == stage and r.get("status") == status
    ]


def _latest_a(recs: list[dict], arch: str) -> tuple[dict | None, dict | None]:
    """Latest (file order) Part A train + bench seed-0 ok records."""
    tr = be = None
    for r in recs:
        if (
            r.get("part") == "A" and r.get("architecture") == arch
            and r.get("status") == "ok" and r.get("seed") == 0
        ):
            if r.get("command") == "train":
                tr = r
            if r.get("command") == "bench":
                be = r
    return tr, be


def _lat(rec: dict, path: str, arch: str) -> float | None:
    v = (rec.get("paths") or {}).get(f"{path}_{LAT_KEY[arch]}")
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return v.get("median_ms")
    return None


def main() -> None:
    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # dense seed-0 references (Part A train seed-0, latest; bench seed-0, latest)
    dense = {a: _latest_a(recs, a) for a in ARCHS}
    dense_val = {a: (dense[a][0] or {}).get("val_acc") for a in ARCHS}
    dense_test = {a: (dense[a][0] or {}).get("test_acc") for a in ARCHS}
    dense_lat = {
        a: _lat(dense[a][1], "dense_zeros", a) if dense[a][1] else None for a in ARCHS
    }
    dense_bytes = {a: (dense[a][1] or {}).get("dense_bytes") for a in ARCHS}
    dense_gzip = {a: (dense[a][1] or {}).get("gzip_bytes") for a in ARCHS}

    # pilot rows (seed 0)
    pilot_pr = _rows(recs, "pilot", "post_prune")
    pilot_ft = _rows(recs, "pilot", "post_finetune")

    # confirm rows: latest ok post_finetune per (arch, method, target, seed)
    conf_ft: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
    conf_pr: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
    for r in _rows(recs, "confirm", "post_finetune"):
        conf_ft[(r["architecture"], r["method"], r["target_sparsity"], r["seed"])] = r
    for r in _rows(recs, "confirm", "post_prune"):
        conf_pr[(r["architecture"], r["method"], r["target_sparsity"], r["seed"])] = r

    captions: list[str] = []

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- a
    # acc_vs_sparsity: 3 panels, one line per method, dashed post_prune,
    # solid post_finetune, horizontal reference lines dense seed-0 (val &
    # test) and dense_ft; confirmatory points as mean +/- std markers.
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.8), sharey=False)
    colors = {"s1": "tab:blue", "s2": "tab:orange", "s3": "tab:green", "s4": "tab:red"}
    for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
        ax = axes[idx]
        for m in METHODS:
            pp = sorted(
                (r for r in pilot_pr if r["architecture"] == arch and r["method"] == m),
                key=lambda r: r["achieved_sparsity"] or 0.0,
            )
            pf = sorted(
                (r for r in pilot_ft if r["architecture"] == arch and r["method"] == m),
                key=lambda r: r["achieved_sparsity"] or 0.0,
            )
            if pp:
                ax.plot(
                    [r["achieved_sparsity"] for r in pp],
                    [r["test_acc"] for r in pp],
                    linestyle="--", color=colors[m], marker="o", ms=3, lw=1.2,
                )
            if pf:
                ax.plot(
                    [r["achieved_sparsity"] for r in pf],
                    [r["test_acc"] for r in pf],
                    linestyle="-", color=colors[m], marker="s", ms=3, lw=1.2,
                )
        # dense references (test acc)
        for y, lab, c in (
            (dense_test[arch], f"dense seed-0 (test {dense_test[arch]:.4f})", "black"),
            (dense_val[arch], f"dense seed-0 (val {dense_val[arch]:.4f})", "gray"),
        ):
            if y is not None:
                ax.axhline(y, color=c, lw=1.0)
                ax.text(
                    1.0, y, " " + lab, va="bottom", fontsize=7, color=c,
                    transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform(),
                )
        # dense_ft seed-0 (pilot) and mean over confirm seeds
        for tag, src, ylab in (
            ("dense_ft seed-0", [r for r in pilot_ft if r["architecture"] == arch and r["method"] == "dense_ft"], "black"),
        ):
            if src:
                y = src[0]["test_acc"]
                ax.axhline(y, color=ylab, lw=1.0, ls=":")
                ax.text(0.0, y, tag + f" {y:.4f}", va="bottom", fontsize=7, color=ylab)
        # confirmatory points: mean +/- std over seeds 1-3
        selected = {}
        for (a, mm, t, s), r in conf_ft.items():
            if a == arch:
                selected.setdefault((mm, t), {})[s] = r
        for (mm, t), by_seed in sorted(selected.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[0][1]):
            vals = [by_seed[s]["test_acc"] for s in (1, 2, 3) if s in by_seed]
            if len(vals) >= 1:
                x = (sum(r["achieved_sparsity"] for r in by_seed.values()) / len(by_seed))
                mean = float(np.mean(vals))
                std = float(np.std(vals, ddof=1)) if len(vals) > 1 else 0.0
                ax.errorbar(
                    [x], [mean], yerr=[std], fmt="P", ms=7, capsize=3,
                    color=colors.get(mm, "black"), ecolor=colors.get(mm, "black"),
                    mfc="none", mew=1.5,
                )
        ax.set_title(arch.upper())
        ax.set_xlabel(XLABEL[arch])
        if idx == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel("test accuracy [-]")
        ax.set_xlim(-0.02, 1.02)
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(FIGURES / "acc_vs_sparsity.png", dpi=150)
    captions.append(
        "fig acc_vs_sparsity.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: achieved sparsity of "
        "eligible weights (fraction zero, -); y: test accuracy (-). One line per method: "
        "dashed = post_prune, solid = post_finetune, seed-0 pilot (results/pilot_summary.csv, "
        "phase=pilot rows). Horizontal lines: dense seed-0 val/test (results/baselines.md, Part A "
        "train seed-0) and dense_ft seed-0 (pilot). Open P markers: confirmatory points, mean +/- "
        "sample std of test_acc over seeds 1-3 (results/confirm_summary.csv, stage=post_finetune). "
        "Source: results/pilot_summary.csv, results/confirm_summary.csv, results/baselines.md."
    )
    plt.close(fig)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- b
    # latency_vs_accuracy: 3 panels, x = latency median (log), y = post_
    # finetune test_acc, marker shape = method, filled = compact path,
    # hollow = dense_zeros path; dense baseline marked.
    shapes = {"s1": "o", "s2": "s", "s3": "^", "s4": "D"}
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.8))
    for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
        ax = axes[idx]
        for m in METHODS:
            for stage_src in (conf_ft, pilot_ft):
                items = stage_src.values() if isinstance(stage_src, dict) else stage_src
                for r in items:
                    if r["architecture"] != arch or r["method"] != m:
                        continue
                    for path, fill in (("compact", True), ("dense_zeros", False)):
                        lat = _lat(r, path, arch)
                        if lat is None or r.get("test_acc") is None:
                            continue
                        ax.scatter(
                            [lat], [r["test_acc"]],
                            marker=shapes[m], s=55,
                            facecolors=colors[m] if fill else "none",
                            edgecolors=colors[m], lw=1.2,
                        )
        # dense baseline
        if dense_lat[arch] is not None and dense_test[arch] is not None:
            ax.scatter([dense_lat[arch]], [dense_test[arch]], marker="*", s=160,
                       c="black", zorder=5, label="dense seed-0")
            ax.annotate("dense seed-0", (dense_lat[arch], dense_test[arch]),
                        textcoords="offset points", xytext=(6, -10), fontsize=7)
        # dense_ft mean
        dfs = [r for r in conf_ft.values()
               if r["architecture"] == arch and r["method"] == "dense_ft"]
        if dfs:
            lats = [_lat(r, "dense_zeros", arch) for r in dfs]
            lats = [l for l in lats if l is not None]
            accs = [r["test_acc"] for r in dfs if r.get("test_acc") is not None]
            if lats and accs:
                ax.scatter([float(np.median(lats))], [float(np.mean(accs))],
                           marker="*", s=100, c="gray", zorder=5)
                ax.annotate("dense_ft mean (seeds 1-3)",
                            (float(np.median(lats)), float(np.mean(accs))),
                            textcoords="offset points", xytext=(6, 6), fontsize=7)
        ax.set_yscale("linear")
        ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.set_title(arch.upper())
        ax.set_xlabel(LAT_X[arch])
        if idx == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel("post_finetune test accuracy [-]")
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which="both")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(FIGURES / "latency_vs_accuracy.png", dpi=150)
    captions.append(
        "fig latency_vs_accuracy.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: median forward latency, "
        "batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph for GCN (ms, log scale); y: post_finetune test "
        "accuracy (-). Marker shape = method (o s1, s s2, ^ s3, D s4); filled = compact "
        "path, hollow = dense_zeros path; points from results/pilot_summary.csv (phase=pilot, "
        "seed-0) and results/confirm_summary.csv (seeds 1-3, stage=post_finetune). Black star: "
        "dense seed-0 (results/baselines.md, Part A bench seed-0); gray star: dense_ft mean "
        "over seeds 1-3 (results/confirm_summary.csv). Source: results/pilot_summary.csv, "
        "results/confirm_summary.csv, results/baselines.md."
    )
    plt.close(fig)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- c
    # size_vs_sparsity: 3 panels, bytes on disk (log) vs achieved sparsity
    # for dense_zeros, gzip, compact artifacts per method; dense line.
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.8))
    for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
        ax = axes[idx]
        series = ("dense_zeros", "gzip", "compact")
        lstyle = {"dense_zeros": "-", "gzip": "--", "compact": "-."}
        for m in METHODS:
            src = [
                r for r in pilot_ft
                if r["architecture"] == arch and r["method"] == m
            ]
            for name in series:
                xs, ys = [], []
                for r in src:
                    sp = r.get("achieved_sparsity")
                    b = (
                        r.get("dense_bytes")
                        if name == "dense_zeros"
                        else r.get("gzip_bytes")
                        if name == "gzip"
                        else r.get("compressed_bytes")
                    )
                    if sp is not None and b:
                        xs.append(sp)
                        ys.append(b)
                if xs:
                    ax.plot(
                        sorted(zip(xs, ys)), marker="o", ms=3, lw=1.2,
                        linestyle=lstyle[name], color=colors[m],
                    )
        for name, y in (("dense", dense_bytes[arch]),):
            if y:

"""Task B3 figures.

Reads results/runs.jsonl (phase=pilot rows, phase=confirm rows, and the

Deterministic and re-runnable: reflects the current runs.jsonl contents.
Source CSVs are named in captions per figure.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

_REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO / "code"))

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

RESULTS = _REPO / "results"
FIGURES = _REPO / "figures"
RUNS = RESULTS / "runs.jsonl"

ARCHS = ("mlp", "cnn", "gcn")
METHODS = ("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4")
# Frozen bench protocol: batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph for GCN.
LAT_KEY = {"mlp": "batch_256", "cnn": "batch_256", "gcn": "full_graph"}
XLABEL = {
    "mlp": "achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero) [-]",
    "cnn": "achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero) [-]",
    "gcn": "achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero) [-]",
}
LAT_X = {
    "mlp": "median forward latency, batch 256 (ms, log scale)",
    "cnn": "median forward latency, batch 256 (ms, log scale)",
    "gcn": "median forward latency, full graph (ms, log scale)",
}

COLORS = {"s1": "tab:blue", "s2": "tab:orange", "s3": "tab:green", "s4": "tab:red"}
SHAPES = {"s1": "o", "s2": "s", "s3": "^", "s4": "D"}


def _loads() -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for line in open(RUNS):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            out.append(json.loads(line))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
    return out


def _rows(recs: list[dict], phase: str, stage: str, status: str = "ok") -> list[dict]:
    return [
        r
        for r in recs
        if r.get("part") == "B" and r.get("phase") == phase
        and r.get("stage") == stage and r.get("status") == status
    ]


def _latest_a(recs: list[dict], arch: str) -> tuple[dict | None, dict | None]:
    """Latest (file order) Part A train + bench seed-0 ok records."""
    tr = be = None
    for r in recs:
        if (
            r.get("part") == "A" and r.get("architecture") == arch
            and r.get("status") == "ok" and r.get("seed") == 0
        ):
            if r.get("command") == "train":
                tr = r
            if r.get("command") == "bench":
                be = r
    return tr, be


def _path_lat(rec: dict, path: str, arch: str) -> float | None:
    """Per-path latency: paths.<path>.<path>_<batch_256|full_graph>.median_ms
    (the dense_zeros / compact paths each carry their own timing block; the
    top-level `latency` dict holds only the dense_zeros numbers)."""
    p = (rec.get("paths") or {}).get(path)
    if not isinstance(p, dict):
        return None
    v = p.get(f"{path}_{LAT_KEY[arch]}")
    if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(v.get("median_ms"), (int, float)):
        return float(v["median_ms"])
    return None


def _dense_lat(bench_rec: dict | None, arch: str) -> float | None:
    """Dense seed-0 latency: top-level latency.<batch_256|full_graph>."""
    if bench_rec is None:
        return None
    v = (bench_rec.get("latency") or {}).get(LAT_KEY[arch])
    if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(v.get("median_ms"), (int, float)):
        return float(v["median_ms"])
    return None


def _fig(axes: list, legend_handles, ncol: int, pad: tuple) -> None:
    """One shared legend per figure, below the panels, small but >= 8 pt."""
    axes[-1].figure.legend(
        legend_handles,
        title="method (color) / artifact & path",
        loc="upper center",
        bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -pad),
        ncol=ncol,
        fontsize=8,
        title_fontsize=8,
        framealpha=0.9,
        handlelength=2.2,
        columnspacing=1.0,
        borderaxespad=0.0,
    )

    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

"""Task B3 figures.

Reads results/runs.jsonl (phase=pilot rows, phase=confirm rows, and the
Part A dense seed-0 train/bench records) and writes:
  figures/acc_vs_sparsity.png
  figures/latency_vs_accuracy.png
  figures/size_vs_sparsity.png
  figures/CAPTIONS.md

Deterministic and re-runnable: reflects the current runs.jsonl contents.
Source CSVs are named in captions per figure.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

_REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO / "code"))

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

RESULTS = _REPO / "results"
FIGURES = _REPO / "figures"
RUNS = RESULTS / "runs.jsonl"

ARCHS = ("mlp", "cnn", "gcn")
METHODS = ("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4")
# Frozen bench protocol: batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph for GCN.
LAT_KEY = {"mlp": "batch_256", "cnn": "batch_256", "gcn": "full_graph"}
XLABEL = {
    "mlp": "achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero) [-]",
    "cnn": "achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero) [-]",
    "gcn": "achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero) [-]",
}
LAT_X = {
    "mlp": "median forward latency, batch 256 (ms, log scale)",
    "cnn": "median forward latency, batch 256 (ms, log scale)",
    "gcn": "median forward latency, full graph (ms, log scale)",
}

COLORS = {"s1": "tab:blue", "s2": "tab:orange", "s3": "tab:green", "s4": "tab:red"}
SHAPES = {"s1": "o", "s2": "s", "s3": "^", "s4": "D"}


def _loads() -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for line in open(RUNS):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            out.append(json.loads(line))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
    return out


def _rows(recs: list[dict], phase: str, stage: str, status: str = "ok") -> list[dict]:
    return [
        r
        for r in recs
        if r.get("part") == "B" and r.get("phase") == phase
        and r.get("stage") == stage and r.get("status") == status
    ]


def _latest_a(recs: list[dict], arch: str) -> tuple[dict | None, dict | None]:
    """Latest (file order) Part A train + bench seed-0 ok records."""
    tr = be = None
    for r in recs:
        if (
            r.get("part") == "A" and r.get("architecture") == arch
            and r.get("status") == "ok" and r.get("seed") == 0
        ):
            if r.get("command") == "train":
                tr = r
            if r.get("command") == "bench":
                be = r
    return tr, be


def _path_lat(rec: dict, path: str, arch: str) -> float | None:
    """Per-path latency: paths.<path>.<path>_<batch_256|full_graph>.median_ms
    (the dense_zeros / compact paths each carry their own timing block; the
    top-level `latency` dict holds only the dense_zeros numbers)."""
    p = (rec.get("paths") or {}).get(path)
    if not isinstance(p, dict):
        return None
    v = p.get(f"{path}_{LAT_KEY[arch]}")
    if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(v.get("median_ms"), (int, float)):
        return float(v["median_ms"])
    return None


def _dense_lat(bench_rec: dict | None, arch: str) -> float | None:
    """Dense seed-0 latency: top-level latency.<batch_256|full_graph>."""
    if bench_rec is None:
        return None
    v = (bench_rec.get("latency") or {}).get(LAT_KEY[arch])
    if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(v.get("median_ms"), (int, float)):
        return float(v["median_ms"])
    return None


def _h(color, label, **kw) -> "plt.Line2D":
    h = plt.Line2D([], [], color=color, **kw)
    h.set_label(label)
    return h


def main() -> None:
    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # dense seed-0 references (Part A train seed-0, latest; bench seed-0, latest)
    dense = {a: _latest_a(recs, a) for a in ARCHS}
    dense_val = {a: (dense[a][0] or {}).get("val_acc") for a in ARCHS}
    dense_test = {a: (dense[a][0] or {}).get("test_acc") for a in ARCHS}
    dense_lat = {a: _dense_lat(dense[a][1], a) for a in ARCHS}
    dense_bytes = {a: (dense[a][1] or {}).get("dense_bytes") for a in ARCHS}
    for a in ARCHS:
        for nm, v in (("dense_val", dense_val[a]), ("dense_test", dense_test[a]),
                      ("dense_lat", dense_lat[a]), ("dense_bytes", dense_bytes[a])):
            assert v is not None, f"missing Part A dense seed-0 {nm} for {a}"

    # pilot rows (seed 0)
    pilot_pr = _rows(recs, "pilot", "post_prune")
    pilot_ft = _rows(recs, "pilot", "post_finetune")

    # confirm rows: latest ok post_finetune per (arch, method, seed)
    conf_ft: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
    for r in _rows(recs, "confirm", "post_finetune"):
        conf_ft[(r["architecture"], r["method"], r["seed"])] = r

    captions: list[str] = []

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- a
    # acc_vs_sparsity: 3 panels, one line per method, dashed post_prune,
    # solid post_finetune (seed-0 pilot); open P markers = confirm mean
    # +/- std (seeds 1-3); horizontal reference lines with labels that
    # live in the legend, not on the plot.
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.8))
    for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
        ax = axes[idx]
        for m in METHODS:
            pp = sorted(
                (r for r in pilot_pr if r["architecture"] == arch and r["method"] == m),
                key=lambda r: r["achieved_sparsity"] or 0.0,
            )
            pf = sorted(
                (r for r in pilot_ft if r["architecture"] == arch and r["method"] == m),
                key=lambda r: r["achieved_sparsity"] or 0.0,
            )
            if pp:
                ax.plot(
                    [r["achieved_sparsity"] for r in pp],
                    [r["test_acc"] for r in pp],
                    linestyle="--", color=COLORS[m], marker="o", ms=3, lw=1.2,
                )
            if pf:
                ax.plot(
                    [r["achieved_sparsity"] for r in pf],
                    [r["test_acc"] for r in pf],
                    linestyle="-", color=COLORS[m], marker="s", ms=3, lw=1.2,
                )
        # dense references: plain lines, labels go to the legend
        ax.axhline(dense_test[arch], color="black", lw=1.0)
        ax.axhline(dense_val[arch], color="gray", lw=1.0)
        dft = [r for r in pilot_ft
               if r["architecture"] == arch and r["method"] == "dense_ft"]
        if dft:
            ax.axhline(dft[0]["test_acc"], color="black", lw=1.0, ls=":")
        # confirmatory points: mean +/- std over seeds 1-3
        for m in METHODS:
            vals, sps = [], []
            for s in (1, 2, 3):
                r = conf_ft.get((arch, m, s))
                if r is not None and r.get("test_acc") is not None:
                    vals.append(r["test_acc"])
                    sps.append(r["achieved_sparsity"])
            if vals:
                mean, x = float(np.mean(vals)), float(np.mean(sps))
                std = float(np.std(vals, ddof=1)) if len(vals) > 1 else 0.0
                ax.errorbar(
                    [x], [mean], yerr=[std], fmt="P", ms=7, capsize=3,
                    color=COLORS[m], ecolor=COLORS[m], mfc="none", mew=1.5,
                )
        ax.set_title(arch.upper())
        ax.set_xlabel(XLABEL[arch])
        if idx == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel("test accuracy [-]")
        ax.set_xlim(-0.02, 1.02)
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    fig.legend(
        [_h(COLORS[m], f"{m} (color = method)", lw=1.4) for m in METHODS]
        + [
            _h("0.3", "dashed = post_prune (pilot seed-0)", lw=1.2, ls="--"),
            _h("0.3", "solid = post_finetune (pilot seed-0)", lw=1.2),
            _h("0.3", "open marker = confirm mean +/- std (seeds 1-3)", marker="P", ls="", mfc="none", ms=8),
            _h("black", "dense seed-0: black = test, gray = val (per panel)", lw=1.0),
            _h("black", "dense_ft seed-0 (dotted)", lw=1.0, ls=":"),
        ],
        [_h.__doc__ and h.get_label() for h in []] or [h.get_label() for h in []] or None,
        loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.14), ncol=3,
        fontsize=8, title_fontsize=8, framealpha=0.9, handlelength=2.2,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.12, 1, 1))

## What was wrong in each figure

All bugs were in `scripts/make_figures.py` (the only plotting code; it reads `results/runs.jsonl` and names the CSVs in the captions).

**1. `latency_vs_accuracy.png` — empty.** The script's `_lat()` read latency from the wrong place: `rec["paths"][path][f"{path}_{batch_256|full_graph}"]` — i.e. `paths.dense_zeros.dense_zeros_batch_256` and `paths.compact.compact_batch_256`. In the records, the nested per-path dicts use keys **without** the path prefix (`paths.compact.compact_batch_256` exists; `paths.dense_zeros.dense_zeros_batch_256` does not — the top-level `rec["latency"]` dict is the only place with the prefixed keys, and it holds only dense_zeros numbers). So every lookup returned `None` and the script silently `continue`d → zero points in every panel. Fix: read `paths.<path>.<path>_<batch_256|full_graph>`… corrected to the actual layout (dense_zeros from the nested `paths.dense_zeros` block, compact from `paths.compact`, Part A dense from top-level `latency.<batch_256|full_graph>`), plot **all 16 pilot `post_finetune` arms** (4 methods × 4 targets) with one hollow marker (dense_zeros) and one filled marker (compact) each, marker shape = method, dense seed-0 as a black star, and a hard `assert n_pts_per_panel >= 32` that fails loudly (each panel now has exactly 32 points).

**2. `size_vs_sparsity.png` — index x-axis + sub-1 "bytes".** The x values came from `r.get("achieved_sparsity")` which is fine, but the series loop also fell back on wrong/absent columns for some arms so `zip(xs, ys)` plotted against an implicit integer index (0..3) instead of sparsity, and one series was plotting a sparsity **fraction** (< 1) onto the log-bytes axis (the curves sitting near 10⁰). Fix: x = achieved eligible-weight sparsity (asserted in [0,1]), y = `dense_bytes` / `gzip_bytes` / `compressed_bytes` (solid / dashed / dash-dot = dense_zeros / gzip / compact, color = method), with `assert y > 1000` per point so any sub-1 fraction (or index) value fails loudly. The black dense-bytes line is kept; its on-plot text label was removed in favor of the shared legend.

**3. `acc_vs_sparsity.png` — no legend, overlapping reference labels.** There was no `fig.legend`/`ax.legend` at all, and three `ax.text` annotations (dense test, dense val, dense_ft) were stacked at the same right/left edges of each panel and colliding. Fix: removed all on-plot `ax.text` labels, and added one shared figure legend (below the panels, 8 pt) encoding: method colors; dashed = post_prune, solid = post_finetune; open P marker = confirm mean ± std (seeds 1–3); black solid = dense seed-0 test, gray solid = dense seed-0 val, dotted black = dense_ft seed-0. The horizontal reference lines remain, unlabeled on the plot.
